summary:
Ogun State in south-west Nigeria has no protective statute of its own for transgender or gender-nonconforming people, and the sources reviewed record no Ogun-specific incident, enforcement action or divergence. The national framework applies in full.

The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office travel advice for Nigeria, as reported by Sahara Reporters on 19 August 2026, warns LGBT+ travellers that they face arrest, violence, blackmail and intimidation, with up to 14 years' imprisonment for same-sex unions under the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014, and death-penalty risk under Sharia criminal law in northern states. Ogun is a southern state and does not fall under Sharia provisions, but the 14-year exposure and the warning of attacks and blackmail apply to visitors in Ogun.

The only trans-specific killing documented in the sources is the case of 'Abuja Area Mama', a 33-year-old transgender TikToker whose beaten body was found on a highway in Abuja on 9 August 2024, as reported by BBC News. She had posted about being transgender and working as a sex worker and had expressed fears for her life the previous year. Police stated that preliminary investigations revealed the individual was a man fully dressed in female clothing. The killing occurred in the federal capital, outside Ogun, and is carried here as national evidence of lethal violence against transgender people; no Ogun-specific incident is documented in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The national advisory frame cited above, warning of attacks, blackmail and intimidation against LGBT+ travellers, is issued for Nigeria as a whole and shapes what a trans visitor should expect in Ogun even though no Ogun-specific enforcement data appears in the sources.

Official police framing in the Abuja Area Mama case, describing a transgender woman as a man in female clothing, indicates how gender-nonconforming people may be characterised by authorities in encounters that could equally occur in Ogun.
localsOnly:
Ogun State residents have no state-level legal protection against discrimination or violence on the basis of gender identity or sexual orientation; the national SSMPA regime and general criminal law govern.

No Ogun-specific enforcement actions, arrests, prosecutions or protective measures for transgender residents are documented in the sources reviewed.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Ogun-specific incident, arrest, enforcement pattern or protective measure for transgender people was identified in the sources; the assessment rests on the national framework and one Abuja incident used as national evidence.

The sources do not resolve how Ogun State police or courts have handled gender-nonconforming individuals in practice, or whether any state-level directives on cross-dressing or presentation have been issued in Ogun.
